summary: Day 1 of the 5-session window went the risk-on way. SPY closed at 759.81 against 749.92 on 11-10, up 1.32% (since_version spy_return +0.0132), with VOO +1.35% and VTI +1.30% on the day. That is already past the +1% grading line, but four sessions remain and one day settles nothing, so the call is ahead, not right. The favored Health Care tilt held up: INCY +1.64% and IDXX +0.64%. Bonds slipped slightly (BND -0.14%, IEF -0.07%) as an equity-up day would suggest, and VNQ was flat (-0.07%). close.json has no QQQ, XLK, RSP, HYG or VIXY data, so I cannot check whether tech joined the rally or whether breadth and credit stayed supportive.
update: Keep risk-on for now. Confidence should go up only if the next packet shows the drivers I named in watch: XLK and QQQ 5-day returns turning positive, RSP 5-day still positive, HYG steady and VIXY not rising. SPY now sits 4.33% above the 728.3 200-day reference (pct_above_stop 0.0433 on VOO/VTI), so the regime cushion is wider than on 11-10. Two cautions for tomorrow. First, Industrials (avoid) did not lag much: FAST rose 0.97% on a 1.32% SPY day, which is one name on one day and not enough to change the tilt. Second, BND and IEF are both NEAR their stops (+1.6% above each). If the next packet shows TLT and IEF falling further over 5 days, that weakens my 'BND is low-risk ballast' line and argues for leaning on cash rather than bonds as the defensive sleeve. The track record point still applies: one strong up day after 11 windows with no +1% week is the kind of move the risk-on call needed, but a reversal over the remaining four sessions would put it back inside +/-1%.
